note: GeoServer can hand back a legend as JSON instead of a picture: rules with colour, quantity and label. That is the radar-style swatch list the panel wants, sourced from the service rather than typed in here - so it cannot go stale the first time NOAA restyles a layer.
Cloud cover, to confirm the JSON legend is not a one-layer accident and to see how many classes a ramp comes back with - which decides whether the list needs two columns.
Light pollution, first choice. NASA GIBS serves the VIIRS Black Marble night lights composite as plain XYZ tiles, no key. Note the path is z/y/x, not z/x/y.
The same layer with `default` for the time dimension, in case the dated path is wrong.
What GIBS actually calls its night-lights layers, read from its own capabilities rather than guessed. Only the ones with a plausible name are printed.

The Lorenz light pollution atlas is the calibrated sky-brightness overlay photographers use, rather than a photograph of streetlights. Its viewer page builds the tile URLs in JavaScript, so this reads the pattern out instead of guessing at it.

NOAA SWPC OVATION 30-minute aurora forecast: a global probability grid. Same shape as the wildfire overlay - no tiles, fetch and render. Watch the byte count; this decides whether it can be fetched on a phone.
Planetary K index, for the Photography panel readout. At Indiana's latitude this is the useful half of aurora forecasting.
Ask BLM what it publishes. GTLF - Ground Transportation Linear Features - carries the OHV designation on every BLM route, and is the biggest single off-road gap in the catalogue.
The USFS Enterprise Data Warehouse folder. Road maintenance level and trail motorized designation live here - the classes and restrictions MVUM alone does not carry.
Tennessee is the next state worth adding. BASEMAPS holds imagery and a topo.
The statewide six-inch mosaic. Answers, but draws nothing over Hardyville where the three-inch does - so it needs a different sublayer or renderer before it is worth offering.
